subtopics.title: What Is Network Security?
subtopics.summary: Introduces the goals of secure communication (confidentiality, message integrity, end-point authentication, availability) and surveys prevalent Internet attacks: eavesdropping/sniffing, message modification, insertion, and deletion, impersonation, session hijacking, and denial of service.

subtopics.title: Principles of Cryptography
subtopics.summary: Fundamental cryptography techniques for encrypting communication, covering both symmetric key and public key encryption, which underpin all secure network protocols.

subtopics.title: Message Integrity and Digital Signatures
subtopics.summary: Techniques for detecting tampering of messages in transit: cryptographic hash functions, message authentication codes (MACs), and digital signatures.

subtopics.title: End-Point Authentication
subtopics.summary: Protocols for verifying the identity of the party with whom one is communicating, using nonces and shared secrets to defeat replay and impersonation attacks.

subtopics.title: Securing E-Mail
subtopics.summary: Application-layer security for e-mail (e.g., PGP), combining digital signatures with symmetric and public key encryption to secure the e-mail message chain.

subtopics.title: Securing TCP Connections: TLS
subtopics.summary: Transport-layer security for TCP connections, covering how TLS provides encryption, message integrity, and end-point authentication, including handshaking and the record protocol.

subtopics.title: Network-Layer Security: IPsec and VPNs
subtopics.summary: Blanket protection at the network layer using the IPsec protocol suite, and its application in building virtual private networks (VPNs).
